# Contributing to MindTape

## Quick Start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mlavrinenko/mindtape.git
cd mindtape
nix develop          # dev shell with the full toolchain (installs the
                     # pre-commit hook: asserts the gate is fresh, checks
                     # task files)
just check           # run before every commit
```

Use `just` recipes rather than raw `cargo`: they carry the right flags and environment, and `just` with no arguments lists them. `flake.nix` owns the tools. In the dev shell `mt` is `target/mt-dev/debug/mt` on `PATH`, not a wrapper that rebuilds: `just build-mt` builds it, `just fork` builds a fresh worktree’s, and `just integrate` rebuilds this checkout’s after the fast-forward. An edit between those events leaves `mt` older than the code beside it until the next build; entering the shell with no binary there names `just build-mt`.

This is the single source for how work is done here; a process rule belongs here and nowhere else. Deep dives sit in `docs/contributing/`, and `AGENTS.md` covers only what MindTape _is_.

## Code Style

All clippy lints are `deny` (workspace `Cargo.toml`); the project will not build with violations. Key restrictions:

- No `unwrap()`/`expect()` outside tests — use `?` with `anyhow`/`thiserror`
- No `todo!()`/`unimplemented!()`/`unreachable!()`/`unsafe`/wildcard imports
- Functions: ≤70 lines, ≤5 args, cognitive complexity ≤20

## Error Handling

- `anyhow::Result` for application code (the CLI); `thiserror::Error` for library error types callers match on (`HarvestError`, `ConfigError`, `FilterError`)
- Keep `main.rs` a thin entry point; logic lives in library modules

## Testing

- Unit tests inline in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` (or a sibling `_tests.rs` via `#[path]`) next to the code they exercise.
- Tests that shell out to the `mt` binary (`assert_cmd::cargo_bin`) belong in `tests/`, not inline: Cargo exports `CARGO_BIN_EXE_mt` before integration tests, a guarantee `--lib` unit tests lack.
- As a file nears the linecop limit, `just fix-check` ejects its inline tests into a `_tests.rs` sibling with [ejectest](https://github.com/mlavrinenko/ejectest).
- Run `just test`; count with `just count-tests`.
- Anything that shells out or joins paths needs a thought for the Windows CI job. What runs there, the `just check-windows` cross-check and the Unix-only pty tests: [docs/contributing/windows.md](docs/contributing/windows.md).
- Mutation testing (`cargo-mutants`) proves whether tests pin behaviour, not just execute it. Run `just mutants-diff` before a PR and triage every survivor: [docs/contributing/mutation-testing.md](docs/contributing/mutation-testing.md).

## Quality Gates (run by `just check`)

| Gate | Command | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fmt-check` | _Check formatting without writing changes (CI-friendly)_ | `cargo fmt` over Rust, `tombi format` over every tracked `*.toml` (`tombi.toml` turns its schema-driven key and array-value sorting off, so a commented group stays where it was written; tombi comes from its own nixpkgs input in `flake.nix`), `typstyle` over the Typst sources, and `--fmt` over the justfiles — the exact path lists are below the table. One list feeds both `fmt` and `fmt-check`, so a path is added in one place, never to a single recipe. The justfiles need a list of their own because a bare `--fmt` formats the root `Justfile` only and silently skips every `mod` file; each file listed gets its own `--justfile <file> --fmt` pass and needs `set unstable := true` of its own, since `--fmt` reads that setting from the file it is pointed at, not from the `Justfile` declaring the `mod`. |
| `clippy` | `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -q -- -D warnings` | Every lint is workspace `deny` (see Code Style above); this recipe runs them. |
| `test` | `cargo nextest run --workspace --status-level fail --cargo-quiet --cargo-quiet "$@"` | The full workspace suite, run through nextest: one process per test, so a panicking or hanging test is isolated, and `--status-level fail` keeps a green run to a header and a summary — only a failure prints, per test, rather than every binary’s own result block. nextest does not run doctests, and there is no separate `cargo test --doc` pass: the tree has none (`cargo test --doc` reports 0 tests in both crates), so a doctest added later must come with a pass of its own. `just test <filter>` (a developer query, no `mmz`) runs this recipe directly with the filter as `ARGS`, so a filtered run never pollutes the cached full-suite record `just check` relies on. |
| `machete` | `cargo machete` | Flags a workspace dependency no crate actually imports. |
| `check-file-size` | `linecop --format paths` | Per-language caps — and the tighter ones on the always-loaded docs — are in [`.linecop.yaml`](.linecop.yaml), argued in place. `linecop --baseline 85` lists what is nearing its cap; run it before adding to an existing file. |
| `check-dry` | _Copy-paste gate: fail on any duplicated Rust block_ | `jscpd` — fails on any duplicated Rust block ≥70 tokens; fix by extracting a shared helper. |
| `check-secrets` | _Fail if the working tree carries a committed credential_ | gitleaks over the working tree under `.gitleaks.toml` — its default ruleset, a walk bound derived on every run from what git ignores (`git ls-files -oi --exclude-standard --directory`, so both `.gitignore` files and the global excludes file count, and a tracked file inside an ignored directory is still scanned; an unbounded scan walks `target/`: 1m44s over 2.09 GB, against 1.5s over 7.5 MB), and one allowlist for the `outdatty.lock` digests `generic-api-key` reads as auth secrets. History is out of scope: `gitleaks git` reports the absolute paths this repo has already committed and would need a `.gitleaksignore` entry per past mint. A control fixture is scanned first and must report an exact set of findings, because “no leaks found” is equally what an over-broad allowlist and a config that loaded no rules print — that one assertion pins the ruleset being live, the derived bound following git’s own negation, the allowlist staying scoped to the rule and to the shape it silences rather than to the whole file, and nothing being wide enough to swallow the tree. A third arm set-differences `git ls-files` against mmz’s own expansion of this rule’s inputs, so the enumeration that stands in for “the whole tree” (`.mmz/config.yaml` has no negative glob, and `truth/tasks/**` may not be named by a gate-tagged rule) fails by name rather than going quietly false-fresh. The bound stops short of one thing: the `lstat` of the bounded directory itself precedes the allowlist check, so the scan holds the `target/www-generated.lock` flock across its walk rather than trusting the bound to stop the `ERR` a concurrent `rm -rf` logs on a run it still exits 0, noise that teaches the reader to skim a security gate. What it cannot do is catch a machine-local path — that is `just crap-baseline-check`’s job, argued there. See `.just/scripts/check-secrets.sh`. |
| `outdatty-check` | `outdatty check --format paths` | See Dependency Drift below for how `outdatty.yaml` couples a source to the dependents it must stay in sync with. |
| `check-examples` | _Validate each example project against itself_ | `mt check` against each example project: `examples/learn-piano/` (full config surface; feeds the docs generator and the skill’s triage evals), `examples/minimal/` (the floor config; feeds the skill’s trap evals), `examples/api-service/` (a backend team’s project the docs capture), `examples/links/`, `examples/estimates/`, `examples/statuses/`, `examples/rules/` and `examples/derived-tags/`, the single-subject fixtures the docs site slices its blocks out of, and `examples/dsl/`, the task AGENTS.md quotes. Keep the recipe and the mmz `examples` scope in step, because mmz re-runs this gate only when a file in that scope changes. An ungated fixture breaks silently. |
| `check-doc-coverage` | _Fail if a visible mt subcommand has no CLI doc entry_ | Set-differences `mt _cli --json`’s reflected command names against `www/utils/cli-notes.typ`’s dict keys; fails naming any visible subcommand with no matching entry, so a new verb cannot ship undocumented. |
| `check-doc-facts` | _Fail if a derived crate, DSL field, framework, gate, or sweep flag fact has no doc entry_ | Regenerates `www/generated/{crate-map,dsl-fields,frameworks,gates,sweep-flags}.json` (`www/generate-facts.sh`) and set-differences each against its `www/utils/{crate-notes,dsl-field-notes,framework-notes,gate-notes,sweep-flag-notes}.typ` prose dict; fails naming any crate, DSL field, priority framework, gate, or sweep flag with no matching entry — this file included. A further arm set-differences the value-taking arguments `cli.json` reflects out of clap against the ones `crates/mindtape-cli/src/completion.rs` names a value source for, so a new completable argument cannot ship silently uncompleted. Both sides come out of the same reflection, so a mention the parser never sees cannot satisfy it; a `ValueEnum` argument is excluded because clap completes a `possible_values` list itself, and “no project value fits” counts as an answer — it is recorded with its reason rather than left blank. |
| `check-doc-recipes` | _Fail on a hand-typed just recipe mention outside the generated module_ | Fails on a hand-typed recipe mention in a doc source — literal `just` followed by a name, whether or not the name is real — that should have gone through the generated module (`www/generated/just.typ`, called as `#just.check()` and friends) instead. The three literal shapes it scans for (a prose backtick span, a fenced example’s leading command, a quoted config value) are argued in place in `.just/scripts/check-doc-recipes.sh`. |
| `check-doc-spans` | _Fail if a doc code span names an unknown mt command, flag or config key_ | Fails when an inline code span names an `mt` subcommand, flag or config key that `mt _cli --json` or `schema/config.schema.json` lacks, so a rename cannot leave the old name in the prose. See `.just/scripts/check-doc-spans.sh`. |
| `check-doc-prose` | _Fail on history words or all-caps emphasis in the doc sources_ | Stops a doc source from telling history or shouting. The rules, with examples, are in [docs/contributing/documentation.md](docs/contributing/documentation.md). |
| `check-doc-blocks` | _Fail on a code block typed by hand into a doc source_ | A code block typed by hand into a doc source shows text nothing runs, so it drifts from what `mt` accepts. This fails, naming file and line, on a fenced block or a block `raw(...)` whose text is written in place. A block comes from a `docs:slice` of a checked fixture, a capture or a derived fact. One no fixture can hold carries `// docs:hand-typed <reason>` on the line above. The script lists the sources not yet converted, and that list only shrinks. See `.just/scripts/check-doc-blocks.sh`. |
| `docs::check` | _Build, index, and validate the docs site_ | `docs-gen` — a dependency — captures live `mt` output first (`www/generate.sh`), so this gate always sees fresh CLI examples before `pagefind` indexes the build for client-side search and `tola validate` checks links and assets. Both `tola` steps print only on failure. |
| `docs::md-check` | _Fail if generated Markdown has drifted from docs/src_ | Regenerates every `docs/src/*.typ` source with typlite into a temp directory and diffs each against the committed Markdown it declares; fails naming any drifted file rather than healing it in place. It also lints each render for shapes GitHub shows broken, naming file and line. `just docs md` refreshes it — see [docs/contributing/generated-docs.md](docs/contributing/generated-docs.md). |
| `fmt-fixture-check` | _Lock the formatter gates against a mis-formatted fixture_ | Synthesizes a deliberately mis-formatted TOML and Typst fixture in a temp directory and asserts `tombi format --check` and `typstyle --check` both reject it (and accept a reformatted one); locks the formatter gates themselves, so a formatter silently accepting drift could not let `fmt-check` pass on an out-of-sync editor save. |
| `arg-pattern-check` | _Lock the arg-attribute patterns against known-bad and known-good input_ | Dispatch-only self-test for the `[arg(...)]` patterns on `just release VERSION`, `just bench N`, `just gen-bench N`, `just eject PCT` and the five `just ask-refactoring` thresholds: asserts each rejects a known-bad argument and accepts a known-good one, and that every declared default satisfies its own pattern (`fix-check` depends on bare `eject`; the sweep’s defaults are the only copy of its thresholds). One of the sweep’s cases is a value containing a space, which the pattern refuses at dispatch, so the recipe never word-splits it. Every assertion goes through the `--dry-run --yes` flag pair, so no recipe body ever actually runs — `release`’s included; see `.just/scripts/arg-pattern-check.sh`. |
| `positional-args-check` | _Lock positional-argument forwarding on the four passthrough recipes_ | Static self-test for the four passthrough recipes — `just test <filter>`, `just build <args>`, `just mutants <args>` and `just mutants-diff <args>` — asserting each carries `[positional-arguments]` and forwards `"$@"` rather than interpolating `{{ ARGS }}` into its body, which would re-split an argument containing a space and re-glob one containing a wildcard. Reads the `--dump --dump-format json` dump and greps the scripts the recipes forward into; no recipe body runs. See `.just/scripts/positional-args-check.sh`. |
| `script-attr-check` | _Lock the script attribute and each justfile's strict-mode interpreter_ | Strict-mode self-test in two arms. No recipe body may open with a `#!` shebang — every script body reaches the interpreter through `[script]`, so `set script-interpreter` applies to it — and every justfile must declare a setting that actually aborts a failed pipeline. `shebang` in the dump cannot tell the two apart (a `[script]` recipe reports `true` exactly as a `#!` body does, measured on just 1.46), so the first arm pairs that field with the absence of a `script` attribute. The second runs a `false \| true` probe under a replica justfile carrying the file’s own setting line verbatim, rather than matching its text: `-euo pipefail` would fail a literal match while being strictly better, and `-e` alone would pass a looser one while dropping the exact flag that let `just count-tests` report a partial sum and exit 0. Every justfile is checked, including one with no `[script]` recipe. A module does not inherit the root’s setting, so `.just/docs.just` keeps its own even though none of its recipes uses it yet; see `.just/scripts/script-attr-check.sh`. |
| `size-fixture-check` | _Lock the size gate's scan scope against an oversized hidden-dir fixture_ | Scan-scope self-test for `just check-file-size`: an oversized shell script at `.just/scripts/` inside a replica tree must be reported by `linecop` reading this repo’s own `.linecop.yaml`, and must go unreported with `include_hidden` deleted from it. The caps need no self-test — a wrong number is visible — but a directory the walker never enters reports the same “All files within size limits.” a clean tree does, which is how every recipe body extracted into `.just/scripts/` sat uncapped while the extraction’s stated reason was bringing them under a cap. Runs against a replica rather than the real directory because `just check` runs its arms in parallel and a probe in the tracked tree would fail the real size gate mid-run; see `.just/scripts/size-fixture-check.sh`. |
| `script-scope-check` | _Lock every gate script into a named mmz scope and outdatty's dev-docs group_ | Enumeration lock over the two manifests that list `.just/scripts/` file by file, in three arms. Every `.just/scripts/*.sh` must be named by some `.mmz/config.yaml` scope as a literal path; every memoized rule whose recipe body reaches a script must declare a scope covering it — the second because a script listed in a scope no rule reads passes the first while still serving a stale hit; and every script must be an `outdatty.yaml` `dev-docs` source or carry an exemption naming the reason no doc restates it. It exists because an enumeration, unlike a `.just/scripts/**` glob, does not cover a new script by itself. A wildcard never counts as naming a script, and the third arm demands a decision rather than membership, because `_nav-diff.sh` is outside that group on purpose and forcing it in would ask for a review of seven dependents no change to it can rot. Arm two walks a call graph (`.just/scripts/_script-graph.sh`), so a body reached one hop further counts: through another script (`_nav-diff.sh`, called from site-pages-fixture-check.sh) and through a nested `just` (check-crap.sh shelling out to `just crap`) alike, both being the same edge into the next body. A wrong edge fails a correct manifest, so the reading is narrow where it can over-read — a `just` counts only at command position, never inside the `echo` hints these scripts use to name a recipe they do not run — and loud where it cannot read at all: an unclassified flag or a target that is not a bare recipe name fails rather than being skipped, since a skipped call is the silent miss the walk exists to remove. `.just/scripts/_script-graph-control.sh` drives it over a synthetic tree carrying every one of those shapes at once, both directions being invisible from the real tree, where a correct answer and a broken reader print the same sentence. See `.just/scripts/script-scope-check.sh`. |
| `site-pages-fixture-check` | _Lock the docs manifest gate against three known-bad fixtures_ | Locks the docs manifest gate itself: two pages declaring the same route, a page with no `<page-meta>` block, and a page missing from `www/utils/site.typ`’s NAV were each demonstrated by hand once, when they landed, and nothing since has proven they still fire. Runs a temp-tree replica’s own copy of `www/generate-site-pages.sh` for the first two (never the working tree — `just check`’s arms run in parallel, so a mutation there would be read as real by a concurrent gate), and pins the third by calling `.just/scripts/_nav-diff.sh` directly against a synthetic pair of route lists rather than driving a whole `just check-doc-facts` regenerate. That script is the set-difference `just check-doc-facts` itself calls, so the thing this gate pins is the thing that actually runs. A positive control asserts the unmutated replica passes, and every case asserts both a non-zero exit and that the failure names the offending page or route, never the exit code alone. It regenerates `www/generated/` itself first (`www/generate.sh`, inside the flock, the snapshot taken before the lock drops) rather than reading what the parallel `just docs gen` arm may have left: that directory is gitignored, so on a cold checkout the replica had no captures to compile against and every case failed for want of them — indistinguishable, on the run that decides, from the gate catching a real break. The replica is copied entry by entry so it can skip `www/public/` and `www/.tola/` — gitignored build outputs no page compile reads, both written by the parallel `just docs check` arm, so copying them made this gate a reader of a tree another arm rewrites underneath it for 8 MB of nothing. An assertion beside the copy fails the gate if either reappears. See `.just/scripts/site-pages-fixture-check.sh`. |
| `check-crap` | _Run the CRAP gate when the lcov is fresh, else skip loudly_ | It runs only against a fresh lcov. Editing any source makes the lcov stale, so it skips on the commits that matter. `just check-full` always runs the CRAP gate. |
| `crap-baseline-check` | _Fail if the CRAP baseline is empty or carries machine-local paths_ | The CRAP arm that never skips: it reads the committed baseline itself rather than the lcov, so no coverage run has to be fresh for it to be right. It fails on an entry carrying a machine-local absolute path — what `just crap-baseline` strips after minting, and what a re-mint by hand puts straight back — and on a baseline scoring no functions at all, which passes the ratchet by reporting every function as new. |
| `check-gate-drift` | _Fail if TOML\_FMT\_PATHS drifts from git, or a gate builds mt without --tests_ | Two facts kept by hand, each read from its source, failing by name. The first is `TOML_FMT_PATHS`, read through just’s `--evaluate` flag rather than a grep of the Justfile, against the TOML files git lists, tracked or not yet added (`git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard '*.toml'`). A new file counts the moment it exists, an ignored one never does, and both a missing and an extra path are reported. The second is the rule argued in docs/contributing/gates.md, “One mt binary, one feature set”: every `cargo build` or `cargo run` of `mindtape-cli` that a `just check` arm reaches must carry `--tests`, or write elsewhere by flag (`--release`, `--target-dir`, `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=`). What an arm reaches is derived, never listed, by `.just/scripts/_script-reach.sh`, which walks the graph `just script-scope-check` already trusts: the recipe names `check` hands to `mmz`, followed through dependencies, a nested `just`, and any script a body or script names, so a script that arrives is read by arriving. That is also why `just check-rrule` is out: it is not an arm, its feature build is the point, and CI runs it serially, after its own nextest has stopped using the binary, so the race needs a test run in flight beside it that it never has. `cargo run` takes no `--tests`, so it passes only by writing elsewhere. A control runs first, because “no findings” is equally what a reader that stopped following edges prints: synthetic trees in a temp directory, one clean (every exempt shape, an unreached recipe, a heredoc, an `echo`) and one carrying a plain build in a recipe, a script, a nested script, a nested recipe and a continuation line, asserting the exact offenders; never the working tree, as `just check` runs its arms in parallel. See `.just/scripts/check-gate-drift.sh`. |

`fmt-check`’s non-Rust path lists:

- `JUST_FMT_PATHS`: `.just/docs.just`
- `TOML_FMT_PATHS`: `.cargo/mutants.toml`, `.config/nextest.toml`, `.gitleaks.toml`, `.mindtape/config.toml`, `Cargo.toml`, `clippy.toml`, `crates/mindtape-cli/Cargo.toml`, `crates/mindtape-cli/src/axes/headers_spec.toml`, `crates/mindtape-cli/src/axes/workflow_flow.toml`, `crates/mindtape-cli/src/axes/workflow_gated.toml`, `crates/mindtape-cli/src/axes/workflow_personal.toml`, `crates/mindtape-cli/src/axes/workflow_todo_done.toml`, `crates/mindtape-cli/src/presets/flow/config.toml`, `crates/mindtape-cli/src/presets/gated/config.toml`, `crates/mindtape-cli/src/presets/personal/config.toml`, `crates/mindtape-cli/src/presets/todone/config.toml`, `crates/mindtape/Cargo.toml`, `crates/mindtape/src/defaults.toml`, `crates/mindtape/src/frameworks.toml`, `crates/mindtape/src/packs/mindtape-tasks.toml`, `examples/api-service/.mindtape/config.toml`, `examples/derived-tags/.mindtape/config.toml`, `examples/dsl/.mindtape/config.toml`, `examples/estimates/.mindtape/config.toml`, `examples/large/.mindtape/config.toml`, `examples/learn-piano/.mindtape/config.toml`, `examples/links/.mindtape/config.toml`, `examples/minimal/.mindtape/config.toml`, `examples/recurring/.mindtape/config.toml`, `examples/rules/.mindtape/config.toml`, `examples/self-validating/.mindtape/config.toml`, `examples/statuses/.mindtape/config.toml`, `lib/typst.toml`, `rust-toolchain.toml`, `rustfmt.toml`, `tombi.toml`, `www/tola.toml`
- `TYPST_FMT_PATHS`: `lib`, `truth`, `.mindtape/templates`, `examples/api-service/tasks`, `examples/api-service/.mindtape/templates`, `examples/derived-tags/api`, `examples/derived-tags/web`, `examples/learn-piano/tasks`, `examples/learn-piano/.mindtape/templates`, `examples/links/tasks`, `examples/recurring/tasks`, `examples/dsl/tasks`, `examples/rules`, `examples/statuses/tasks`, `www/content`, `www/templates`, `www/utils`, `docs/src`

Every arm runs through `mmz`, so a re-run skips each one whose declared inputs are unchanged and the pre-commit hook can assert the whole set fresh without re-running it. That memoization and the locked formatter gates are in [docs/contributing/gates.md](docs/contributing/gates.md); the gated example projects, in [docs/contributing/example-projects.md](docs/contributing/example-projects.md).

`just check-full` is `just check` plus `just cover` and `just crap`: always correct about coverage and CRAP, at the price of an instrumented rebuild and a full suite pass. Run it before opening a PR, plain `just check` while iterating.

`just fork <slug> <base>` stands one of those worktrees up and `just integrate <branch>` takes it back down. `fork` branches off `<base>` (default `HEAD`) at `../mindtape-<slug>`, `direnv allow`-ed, refusing a dirty `HEAD` — `git worktree add` copies commits, never the working tree — and reporting, without refusing, a divergent base. Fork first, before flipping anything: `main` is still clean at that point, so the worktree never needs a status flip committed there just to clear the refusal — `mt wip <stem>` runs inside the new worktree instead, and its flip lands in the worktree’s first work commit (see Commit Messages). `integrate` refuses unless that worktree reports `mmz --is-fresh --tag gate`, naming the stale arm, then fast-forwards and removes it: a fast-forward writes no commit, so the pre-commit hook never fires on the merge. `fork` also builds the new worktree’s `mt`, once, after loading its shell, and `integrate` rebuilds this checkout’s after the fast-forward, so the binary each `PATH` serves matches the tree it sits in. What each refuses and deliberately leaves undone — no seeded `target/`, no re-run gate, no waiver flag — is argued in `.just/scripts/fork.sh` and `.just/scripts/integrate.sh`.

A delegated worktree whose full aggregate runs at integration can scope the gate with `MINDTAPE_GATE_SCOPE=<reason> git commit`, which demands a matching `Gate-Scope:` trailer; dodging a red gate is never legitimate. When scoping is, and what the trailer buys, are in [docs/contributing/gates.md](docs/contributing/gates.md).

Coverage and CRAP run outside `just check`: run `just cover` first (`just crap` refuses a stale lcov), and `just crap-baseline` in the same commit as any deliberate complexity. The thresholds and every argument behind them, to read before changing either recipe’s flags, are in [docs/contributing/coverage-crap.md](docs/contributing/coverage-crap.md); the baseline’s own paths and guards, in [docs/contributing/crap-baseline.md](docs/contributing/crap-baseline.md).

`just nix-build` verifies `nix build` in a clean sandbox (no dev shell, no sccache). Run it when touching `flake.nix` or `.cargo/config.toml`; `just release` calls it automatically.

## Signal Sweep (`just ask-refactoring`)

The sweep reads the _advisory_ quality signals and files a backlog task per finding. It is not a gate: a gate stops you at the wall, the sweep names the wall you are walking toward. Run it dry (`just ask-refactoring`) to see what it would file; the arms, the scoring and the design rules are in [docs/contributing/signal-sweep.md](docs/contributing/signal-sweep.md).

A delegated agent that notices something real outside its own task’s scope files it the same way — `mt add --template finding`, tagged `found` — before writing the closing report, never in prose alone: the report reaches one reader once, a filed task does not.

## Dependency Drift (outdatty)

[`outdatty.yaml`](outdatty.yaml) couples source files to the dependents that must stay in sync (e.g. the CLI surface to `README.md`). After editing a source, update the listed dependents, re-record the group you touched with `just outdatty-update <group>` and commit `outdatty.lock`. A recorded hash is a review watermark, so blanket re-recording — `just outdatty-update-all` — claims a review that never happened. It stays the explicit choice, never the default.

Edit a dependent alone, and record just that file in the same commit — `just outdatty-update <group> <path>` leaves the group’s other pending dependents pending. Only a source change is a trigger, so the hash would otherwise ride along on an unrelated commit; the reasoning and the pending-groups one-liner are in `outdatty.yaml`’s header.

## Version Management

- No backward compatibility before the first public release: a rename lands whole, callers and configs included, with no alias or migration path left.
- Workspace crates: `Cargo.toml` `[workspace.package] version` (semver).
- Typst library: `lib/typst.toml` `version`, independent of the crates. Several files repeat it and all have to move together; the `typst-pkg-version` outdatty group enumerates them and fails the build otherwise. Trust the group, not a list here.
- `mindtape-cli`’s dependency on `mindtape` carries a version requirement (not path-only), because crates.io rejects path-only deps on publish; bump it with the workspace version.
- A release (`just release VERSION`) is gated twice: an `[arg(...)]` pattern rejects a `v`-prefixed or non-semver `VERSION`, then the body requires the tag to equal the workspace version, a clean tree, and no non-empty `[Unreleased]` section in `CHANGELOG.md` (it moves into a dated section at release time). `main` is pushed before the tag, so the docs site (`pages.yml`) and CI run on the release tree.

## Commit Messages

Conventional Commits in the language of prior commits, with a `Refs: <stem>` footer naming the driving task; a commit that only files or edits task artifacts carries none, and a status flip rides with the work it claims. The rule, the hooks that check it and the two setups are in [docs/contributing/commit-messages.md](docs/contributing/commit-messages.md).

## Command Semantics (read/write separation)

Read commands never mutate the authored tree; only explicit write commands do. Which verb is which, the per-command read test, and the CLI command list it is read from are in [docs/contributing/command-semantics.md](docs/contributing/command-semantics.md).

## Documentation

Docs live in `www/content/*.typ` and the `docs/src/*.typ` Markdown sources. Rewrite a touched file whole, state each fact once, use checked examples, and write plain prose. The rules with examples, and the `just dup-prose` audit, are in [docs/contributing/documentation.md](docs/contributing/documentation.md). Why the site build always rebuilds clean is in [docs/contributing/docs-site-build.md](docs/contributing/docs-site-build.md).

## Extending MindTape

- New CLI command: add `crates/mindtape-cli/src/<name>.rs` with an `Args` struct and a `run` fn; wire it into `cli.rs`. See `ls.rs` for reference.
- New domain capability: add to `crates/mindtape` and re-export from its `lib.rs`. Keep `typst-harvest` consumer-blind — no task concepts there.
- Architectural/tooling decisions: file a task under `truth/tasks/`; there are no ADRs.
